subject.title: [Bug]: Local memory indexer (llama-cpp-provider) hangs indefinitely at 0 chunks

question: Should this stay in maintainer investigation until a real local GGUF indexing run proves the hang boundary, or should ClawSweeper queue a source-only repair attempt now?
rationale: Current source maps the report to an active worker path, but the repo already has timeout and abort scaffolding and the issue is labeled for live reproduction/no new fix PR, so choosing a repair layer without proof could target the wrong boundary.

options.title: Require live GGUF proof first
options.body: Keep this manual until a maintainer or investigator captures a redacted `openclaw memory index --force` run showing whether the worker, node-llama call, timeout, or commit path is stuck.

options.title: Queue source-only worker repair
options.body: Let automation attempt a narrow worker-abort or diagnostics patch from source inspection, accepting a higher chance of an unproven fix.

options.title: Track under HTTP batch hang
options.body: Treat the OpenAI-compatible batch hang as canonical only if a repro proves both failures share the same memory-core batch root cause.

recommendation.title: Require live GGUF proof first
recommendation.body: Keep this manual until a maintainer or investigator captures a redacted `openclaw memory index --force` run showing whether the worker, node-llama call, timeout, or commit path is stuck.

likelyOwner.reason: The worker sidecar and llama.cpp provider boundary history make this the strongest routing candidate for the proof/repair-layer decision.
